definitions.explanation: A safety device that automatically interrupts electrical flow when it detects an overload or short circuit. Located in the breaker box/electrical panel of buildings.

examples.japanese: ブレーカーが{落|お}ちた。
ブレーカーを{上|あ}げてください。
examples.english: Please flip the breaker back on.

examples.japanese: エアコンとドライヤーを{同時|どうじ}に{使|つか}うとブレーカーが{落|お}ちる。
examples.english: The breaker trips if you use the air conditioner and hair dryer at the same time.

notes:
LOANWORD:
From English "breaker" (short for circuit breaker)

HOW IT WORKS:
ブレーカー automatically "trips" ({落|お}ちる) when:
- Too many appliances draw power simultaneously
- {過電流|かでんりゅう} - overcurrent detected
- {漏電|ろうでん} - electrical leak detected
- {短絡|たんらく}/ショート - short circuit occurs

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ブレーカーが{落|お}ちる - breaker trips/goes off
- ブレーカーを{上|あ}げる - to flip breaker back on
- ブレーカーを{下|さ}げる - to turn breaker off
- ブレーカーを{確認|かくにん}する - to check the breaker

TYPES IN JAPANESE HOMES:
- {漏電|ろうでん}ブレーカー - ground fault breaker (main)
- {安全|あんぜん}ブレーカー - safety breaker (individual circuits)
- アンペアブレーカー - amperage breaker (contract capacity)

TROUBLESHOOTING:
If ブレーカー keeps tripping:
1. Reduce number of appliances in use
2. Check for damaged cords
3. Call an electrician if problem persists
